title: Comparing Linear and RBF SVMs on Concentric Circles
description: Generate concentric-circle data with make_circles, fit both LinearSVC and an RBF SVC inside scaled pipelines, and compare their classification reports, confusion matrix, and ROC AUC.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Import scikit-learn SVM and metric modules and generate concentric-circle points with `make_circles` using the supplied sample count, factor, and noise. Split `(X, y)` into training `(Xtr, ytr)` and test `(Xte, yte)` sets using the supplied ratio.

Define two pipelines that each start with `StandardScaler()`. `lin_clf` uses `LinearSVC` with `C=1.0` and the supplied iteration limit; `rbf_clf` uses `SVC(C=1.0, gamma="scale", kernel="rbf", probability=True)`. Fit both on `(Xtr, ytr)`.

Compare the dataset geometry on line 13 with the two classifiers on lines 17-26. `make_circles` places one class inside the other, and `lin_clf` can only draw a straight line in 2D. `rbf_clf` uses radial basis functions (`kernel="rbf"`) to curve around the inner circle.

steps.question: How will `lin_clf` (a straight-line separator) and `rbf_clf` (an RBF kernel separator) compare in test accuracy on the 200 concentric-circle test points?
steps.answer: `lin_clf` gets near-random accuracy (`0.48`), whereas `rbf_clf` separates the inner and outer rings with `0.91` accuracy (`AUC: 0.9649`).

steps.description: Print both `classification_report` tables, display the confusion matrix for `rbf_clf`, and use `rbf_clf.predict_proba(Xte)[:, 1]` with `roc_curve` and `auc` to print `AUC: 0.9649`.
